description: The kinds of findings of the rules of sisakulint (sisakulint/findings/v0): what the args of a finding in a report are. Each member of $defs whose name has a dot is a kind, <rule>.<kind>: an object whose kind is the name and whose other properties are its arguments. x-detected is the text of what the finding says is detected: {name} stands for the argument name, an array is joined by a comma and a space, and any other brace is itself. x-consequence is why it is bad, and x-remedy what a person does about it: each the same text for every finding of the kind, with no argument. x-text on an enumeration is the text of each value in x-detected. The args of a finding are what to read; what is detected is made of them, for people. It refers to facts-v0.json, which is to be in the same directory.

action-list.unlisted.description: A uses of an action or a reusable workflow of another repository that repo.action-list does not allow.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

action-list.unlisted.x-detected: {uses} is not allowed by repo.action-list: {uses}, read as GitHub reads a uses (with empty parts and . dropped, and .. resolved), matches no pattern of repo.action-list, or matches a pattern of repo.action-list that starts with !
action-list.unlisted.x-consequence: the maintainer of the action or of the reusable workflow decides the code that runs, though the repository did not list the action or the reusable workflow as one that the repository trusts: the code of an action runs in the job with the secrets and the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job, and the jobs of a reusable workflow run with the GITHUB_TOKEN of the run and the secrets that the calling job passes
action-list.unlisted.x-remedy: when the repository trusts the maintainer of the action or the reusable workflow, add a pattern that matches the uses to repo.action-list; otherwise, replace the uses with a uses of an action or a reusable workflow that repo.action-list allows

action-list.unlisted-image.description: A uses of a Docker image (docker://), or the image of the container of a job, that repo.action-list does not allow.

uses.description: docker:// and the image, as written in the uses or in the container of the job, or as the matrix gives the image.

action-list.unlisted-image.x-detected: {uses} (a docker:// uses, or docker:// followed by the image of the container of the job) is not allowed by repo.action-list: {uses}, compared as written, matches no pattern of repo.action-list, or matches a pattern of repo.action-list that starts with !
action-list.unlisted-image.x-consequence: the publisher of the image decides what the image holds, though the repository did not list the image as one that the repository trusts: a docker:// step runs the image with the workspace of the job and the environment variables and inputs that the step passes, and the steps of a job whose container is the image run in the image with the secrets and the GITHUB_TOKEN that the steps hold
action-list.unlisted-image.x-remedy: when the repository trusts the publisher of the image, add a pattern that matches the uses to repo.action-list; otherwise, replace the uses with a uses that repo.action-list allows

action-list.unlisted-service.description: The image of a service of a job that repo.action-list does not allow.

uses.description: docker:// and the image of the service, as written, or as the matrix gives the image.

action-list.unlisted-service.x-detected: {uses}, the image of the service {service}, is not allowed by repo.action-list: {uses}, compared as written, matches no pattern of repo.action-list, or matches a pattern of repo.action-list that starts with !
action-list.unlisted-service.x-consequence: the publisher of the image decides what the service runs, though the repository did not list the image as one that the repository trusts: the service reads the environment variables of the service and what the job sends to the service, and sends its responses to the job
action-list.unlisted-service.x-remedy: when the repository trusts the publisher of the image, add a pattern that matches docker:// and the image to repo.action-list; otherwise, replace the image with one that repo.action-list allows

agent-action.description: An action that runs an AI agent.

agent-input.description: An input of an agent action, by the name that the action.yml of the action gives the input.

The flags claude-code-action and its base-action pass to the CLI.

The flags codex-action passes to the CLI.

ai-action-excessive-tools.auto-mode.description: A step of claude-code-action or its base-action whose agent starts in auto mode, or in plan mode, where a classifier, not the permissions, decides the commands it runs: by --permission-mode or defaultMode, or by a third-party provider or a variable of env that keeps Claude Code from fetching its feature flags.

source.description: What decides the mode, as written: a flag, a key of the settings, an input or a variable of env.

ai-action-excessive-tools.auto-mode.x-detected: {source} starts the agent of {action} in a mode where a classifier, not its permissions, decides what runs
ai-action-excessive-tools.auto-mode.x-consequence: an agent an attacker's text steers runs their commands unless the classifier stops them, with the run's token, the secrets in its env, the token actions/checkout leaves in .git/config and, with the sudo of GitHub-hosted runners, the job's secrets in the runner's memory, and sends them out
ai-action-excessive-tools.auto-mode.x-remedy: start the agent in a mode that runs only what its permissions allow (--permission-mode dontAsk, which denies each tool call that the allowed tools do not allow, with the tools the task needs), or run it only on events whose payload holds only what those who can write wrote

ai-action-excessive-tools.run-code.description: A permission of a step of an agent action that lets the agent run any code it chooses: a shell, a command that runs another or reads code with arguments it chooses, or one that runs the workspace's code with an edit of the workspace.

tool.description: The permission that allows the tool, as written in the workflow or in the action.

ai-action-excessive-tools.run-code.x-detected: {tool} lets the agent of {action} run any code it chooses
ai-action-excessive-tools.run-code.x-consequence: an agent an attacker's text steers runs their commands, with the run's token, the secrets in its env, the token actions/checkout leaves in .git/config and, with the sudo of GitHub-hosted runners, the job's secrets in the runner's memory, and sends them out
ai-action-excessive-tools.run-code.x-remedy: allow only the commands the task needs, with their arguments fixed, and, when the agent has a tool that edits files, do not allow a shell, an interpreter or a build; or run the agent only on events whose payload holds only what those who can write wrote

ai-action-excessive-tools.send-network.description: A permission of a step of an agent action that lets the agent send to a host it chooses: a fetch of any URL, or a command with a * that sends.

tool.description: The permission that allows the tool, as written in the workflow or in the action.

ai-action-excessive-tools.send-network.x-detected: {tool} lets the agent of {action} send to a host it chooses
ai-action-excessive-tools.send-network.x-consequence: an attacker's text makes the agent send what it reads, the files of the workspace and of the runner, to the attacker's host
ai-action-excessive-tools.send-network.x-remedy: allow fetching only from fixed domains (WebFetch(domain:…)), or not at all

ai-action-excessive-tools.setting-value.description: A ${{ }} an attacker controls, in an input of an agent action that the action splits into flags or reads as JSON: claude_args, codex-args, settings, copilot-allow-tools.

expr_ref.description: The ${{ }} as written.

ai-action-excessive-tools.setting-value.x-detected: {expr_ref} in {input} of {action} lets an attacker add flags or keys to the agent's settings
ai-action-excessive-tools.setting-value.x-consequence: closing the quote around the value, the attacker allows the agent any tool or takes its sandbox off, and the agent need not follow them
ai-action-excessive-tools.setting-value.x-remedy: keep what an attacker writes out of the setting inputs: give it to the agent as text, through the prompt or env, behind the action's check of the actor

ai-action-excessive-tools.write-token.description: A permission of a step of an agent action that lets the agent write with the token to a target it chooses: a command with a * that writes, a tool of github-mcp-server that writes, or claude-code-action's tag mode push.

tool.description: The permission that allows the tool, as written in the workflow or in the action.

ai-action-excessive-tools.write-token.x-detected: {tool} lets the agent of {action} write with the token where it chooses
ai-action-excessive-tools.write-token.x-consequence: an attacker's text makes the agent comment, label, push or merge wherever the token can write, not only on what it works on
ai-action-excessive-tools.write-token.x-remedy: fix the target in the permission (no *), use tools whose target the action fixes (claude-code-action's use_commit_signing), or give the step a token that writes only what the task needs

ai-action-execution-order.edited-code.description: A step of an agent action whose agent edits the workspace, followed in its job by a step that runs the workspace's code, or git when the agent may write .git.
ai-action-execution-order.edited-code.x-detected: a step after {action} runs the code its agent can edit
ai-action-execution-order.edited-code.x-consequence: an agent an attacker's text steers edits a script, a build or a hook, and the later step runs it with what the job holds: its token, its secrets, the network and the runner's sudo
ai-action-execution-order.edited-code.x-remedy: run the agent as the last step of a job of its own, and pass its output to a new job; or check out the workspace again before a step runs its code

ai-action-execution-order.later-secrets.description: A step of an agent action whose agent runs any code without sudo, followed in its job by a step that holds secrets the agent does not, which what the agent leaves on the runner reaches.
ai-action-execution-order.later-secrets.x-detected: a step after {action} holds secrets its agent does not
ai-action-execution-order.later-secrets.x-consequence: an agent an attacker's text steers leaves a process, a BASH_ENV or a PATH in the environment files, or another action's source, and the later step runs it with its secrets
ai-action-execution-order.later-secrets.x-remedy: run the agent as the last step of a job of its own, and pass its output to a new job; keep the secrets of the steps after it out of that job

ai-action-prompt-injection.env.description: A ${{ }} an attacker controls, in an env of a step of an agent action, which the agent reads through its tools.

expr_ref.description: The ${{ }} as written.

ai-action-prompt-injection.env.x-detected: {expr_ref} in env {env} of {action} gives the agent what an attacker wrote
ai-action-prompt-injection.env.x-consequence: the agent reads the env through its tools, as the workflow means it to, and the attacker's text in it steers the agent with the run's token and its API key
ai-action-prompt-injection.env.x-remedy: keep what an attacker writes out of the agent: run it only on events whose payload holds only what those who can write wrote, and allow it only the tools the task needs

ai-action-prompt-injection.prompt.description: A ${{ }} an attacker controls, in an input an agent action writes into the agent's prompt.

expr_ref.description: The ${{ }} as written.

ai-action-prompt-injection.prompt.x-detected: {expr_ref} in {input} of {action} puts what an attacker wrote into the agent's prompt
ai-action-prompt-injection.prompt.x-consequence: the attacker's text steers the agent over the workflow's prompt: it runs what the step lets it run, with the run's token and the agent's API key, and writes what it is told to
ai-action-prompt-injection.prompt.x-remedy: keep what an attacker writes out of the agent: run it only on events whose payload holds only what those who can write wrote, give it the number of the issue and not its text, and allow it only the tools the task needs; moving the value into env does not help, as the agent reads it there

ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-bot.description: A step of claude-code-action whose allowed_bots is '*' or the actor of a run the attacker triggers: a GitHub App anyone makes starts the agent.

gate_value.description: The value of allowed_bots as written: '*', or a ${{ }} that is the actor of a run the attacker triggers.

ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-bot.x-detected: allowed_bots of {action} is '{gate_value}', which lets any bot start the agent
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-bot.x-consequence: a GitHub App anyone makes opens an issue or comments on a public repository, and its bot starts the agent with a prompt it writes, past the check of the actor
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-bot.x-remedy: list the bots you trust in allowed_bots, not '*' nor a value that is the run's actor, or leave it out

ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-user.description: A step of an agent action that lets any user start the agent: claude-code-action's allowed_non_write_users with a github_token, or codex-action's allow-users, that is '*' or the actor of a run the attacker triggers.

input.description: The input of the action that decides who may start the agent.

gate_value.description: The input's value as written: '*', or a ${{ }} that is the actor of a run the attacker triggers.

ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-user.x-detected: {input} of {action} is '{gate_value}', which lets anyone start the agent
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-user.x-consequence: anyone who opens an issue or comments starts the agent with the run's token and the agent's API key, and the prompt they write steers it
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.any-user.x-remedy: list the users who may start the agent, not '*' nor a value that is the run's actor, or leave the input out so that only those who can write start it

ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.labeler-t.description: A step of an agent action in a job on pull_request_target on labeled, where a workflow of the same repository adds the label that the job waits for to the pull request of an attacker, with actions/labeler and the token of an account: the actor of the labeled run is the account of the token, and the account has write access to the repository, so the action starts the agent.
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.labeler-t.x-detected: the job of {action} runs on pull_request_target on labeled, and actions/labeler in {labeler} is configured to add the label that the job waits for to the pull request of an attacker, with the token of an account; the actor of the labeled run is the account of the token, and the account has write access to the repository, so {action} starts the agent for the run: {action} checks no actor, or {action} checks the actor and lets in an account that has write access
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.labeler-t.x-consequence: an attacker who opens a pull request from a fork starts the agent with no person approving the run; the agent reads the pull request that the attacker wrote, and the agent has the GITHUB_TOKEN of the labeled run and the API key of the agent
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.labeler-t.x-remedy: give actions/labeler the GITHUB_TOKEN, as a label that the GITHUB_TOKEN adds starts no workflow run; or start the agent only on a label that a person adds, a label that no workflow of the repository adds

ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.unchecked.description: A step of an agent action that checks no actor, on an event an outsider triggers.
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.unchecked.x-detected: {action} checks no actor, and the step runs on an event an outsider triggers
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.unchecked.x-consequence: anyone who opens an issue or comments starts the agent with the run's token and its API key
ai-action-unrestricted-trigger.unchecked.x-remedy: limit who starts the agent: run the agent only on events whose payload has nothing an attacker wrote, with a fixed prompt (workflow_dispatch, whose payload the one who dispatches the workflow writes only in the inputs, with a prompt that reads no input), on a label that a maintainer adds, check the actor in the job's if, or use claude-code-action, which checks the actor of the run. The check of the actor does not check the author of the text that the agent reads: the issue that a maintainer labels may still have text that the attacker wrote, so do not put such text in the prompt; ai-action-prompt-injection reports such text

ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.commands.description: A setting of an agent action that takes off the limits on the commands the agent runs: its sandbox or its checks of permissions.

value.description: The word in the value of the input that lets the agent run any command.

ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.commands.x-detected: {value} in {input} of {action} lets the agent run any command
ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.commands.x-consequence: an agent that text an attacker wrote steers runs any command on the runner, with the network: it reads and sends out the token and the secrets of the step
ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.commands.x-remedy: keep the sandbox (codex: workspace-write or read-only) and the checks of permissions (claude: allowedTools for what the task needs)

ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.privileges.description: A setting of an agent action that keeps the privileges of the agent's process: codex-action's safety-strategy unsafe.
ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.privileges.x-detected: {input} {value} of {action} leaves the agent its sudo
ai-action-unsafe-sandbox.privileges.x-consequence: an agent that text an attacker wrote steers reads the API key from memory with sudo and prints it, and the steps after it keep sudo

allowed-actions.failed-job.description: A uses of a step of a composite action that the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) does not allow.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

allowed-actions.failed-job.x-detected: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) does not allow {uses}, a uses of a step of a composite action, when {uses} is read as GitHub reads a uses (with empty parts and the path parts "." dropped, and the path parts ".." resolved, so that owner//repo/./path@v1 is read as owner/repo/path@v1)
allowed-actions.failed-job.x-consequence: GitHub fails the job that runs the composite action in the step "Set up job", before any step of the job runs, and the job shows the error in its log; the jobs whose needs does not name the failed job still run
allowed-actions.failed-job.x-remedy: ask an administrator of the repository, or of the organization that owns the repository, to allow the uses in the setting of allowed actions, or replace the uses with a uses that the setting allows

allowed-actions.unpinned-action.description: A uses of an action by a tag or a branch, where the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) requires a full commit SHA.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

allowed-actions.unpinned-action.x-detected: {uses} names an action by a tag or a branch, not by a full commit SHA, and the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) requires a full commit SHA for each action (sha_pinning_required). This kind does not apply to a uses of a reusable workflow or of a Docker image, which may name a tag under the setting
allowed-actions.unpinned-action.x-consequence: GitHub fails the job of the uses in the step "Set up job", before any step of the job runs, and the job shows the error in its log; the jobs whose needs does not name the failed job still run
allowed-actions.unpinned-action.x-remedy: name the action by the full commit SHA of the commit that the tag or the branch names, such as owner/repo@ followed by the 40 hexadecimal digits of the SHA

allowed-actions.unstarted-run.description: A uses of an action, of a reusable workflow or of a Docker image (docker://) that the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) does not allow, in a workflow or in a reusable workflow that a workflow calls.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

allowed-actions.unstarted-run.x-detected: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) does not allow {uses}, when {uses} is read as GitHub reads a uses (with empty parts and the path parts "." dropped, and the path parts ".." resolved, so that owner//repo/./path@v1 is read as owner/repo/path@v1; a Docker image is compared as written)
allowed-actions.unstarted-run.x-consequence: GitHub does not start the run of the workflow: no job of the run runs, even the jobs that do not use the action, the reusable workflow or the image, and only the page of the run shows the error. GitHub checks the uses before the run starts, so a step whose if is false does not avoid the error
allowed-actions.unstarted-run.x-remedy: ask an administrator of the repository, or of the organization that owns the repository, to allow the uses in the setting of allowed actions, or replace the uses with a uses that the setting allows

approval.description: What makes a person approve a run before the run checks out the code of a pull request.

oneOf.description: The job runs only when a label is added to the pull request: pull_request_target on labeled alone.
The job has a deployment environment with required reviewers.

archived-uses.archived-repository.description: A uses of an action or a reusable workflow of a repository that is archived.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

archived-uses.archived-repository.x-detected: {uses} names {repo}, a repository that is archived
archived-uses.archived-repository.x-consequence: an archived repository is read-only and is no longer maintained: when an error or a vulnerability is found in the action or the reusable workflow, the repository gets no fixed version, and the runner still runs the version that the uses names (the rule known-vulnerable-actions of this linter reports an advisory of the GitHub Advisory Database about the action)
archived-uses.archived-repository.x-remedy: replace the action or the reusable workflow with one that is maintained, or fork the repository, maintain the fork, and point the uses to the fork

args.description: The args of a finding: one of the kinds.

argument-injection.option.description: A value an attacker controls begins a word a command of a run gets, where the command reads a word that begins with - as an option, and the command has an option seen to run a program written in the attacker's spelling.

command.description: The command and the subcommands of the command, such as tar or git fetch.

options.description: The options of the command that run a program, as the attacker writes the options: for one word that holds both the option and the program, a long option with = (--to-command=) or a short option followed by the program in the same word (-e<script>); for two words, the option and then the program, a short option as a word by itself (-c).

expr_ref.description: The reference whose value begins the word, such as github.event.pull_request.title.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the expression, each event named once.

argument-injection.option.x-detected: {command} gets a word that starts with the value of {expr_ref}, or, when the value is outside quotes or is a ${{ }} that the runner writes into the script before the shell reads the script, a word that starts after a blank in the value; an attacker controls the value of {expr_ref} on {controlled_on}; the word is at a place in the order of the words of {command} where {command} reads a word that starts with - as an option (a place before a word such as -- that ends the options), and the attacker can write at that place an option in the list {options}, which makes {command} run a program or code that is written after the name of the option
argument-injection.option.x-consequence: the attacker makes the attacker's value start with the name of one of the options that the finding names, followed by a program; the command reads the word as the option whose name starts the word, and runs the program in the step, with whatever the step can reach, such as the secrets and the token in its env, the credentials actions/checkout leaves in .git/config, the network, and sudo on a GitHub-hosted runner
argument-injection.option.x-remedy: A variable of env and double quotes ("$X") stop the shell from running the value as code, but the variable and the quotes do not stop the command from reading the value as an option. In either fix below, keep the value in the variable of env, and pass the variable to the command inside double quotes. Then either put the word that ends the command's options (--; --end-of-options for git) after the last option the command needs and before the value, for example right before the value (tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt -- "$X"), so that the command reads every word after that word as a plain argument; or, before the command, end the step with an error when the value starts with -, such as [[ $X != -* ]] || exit 1 for the variable X that holds the value. The shell check [[ $X != -* ]] works only when the command gets the value inside double quotes: when the command gets the value outside quotes, a blank in the value starts a new word, and the new word can start with -. For make, -- is not enough: make reads a word of the form NAME=value as the assignment of a variable even after --, so for make end the step with an error when the value starts with - or contains =, such as [[ $X != -* && $X != *=* ]] || exit 1

argument-injection.wiki.description: A value an attacker controls on gollum alone begins a word a command of a run gets, where the command reads a word that begins with - as an option, and the command has an option seen to run a program written in the attacker's spelling: the finding holds if anyone may edit the wiki.

command.description: The command and the subcommands of the command, such as tar or git fetch.

options.description: The options of the command that run a program, as the attacker writes the options: for one word that holds both the option and the program, a long option with = (--to-command=) or a short option followed by the program in the same word (-e<script>); for two words, the option and then the program, a short option as a word by itself (-c).

expr_ref.description: The reference whose value begins the word, such as github.event.pull_request.title.

argument-injection.wiki.x-detected: {command} gets a word that starts with the value of {expr_ref}, and an attacker controls the value on gollum alone; for the name of a wiki page (page_name), GitHub makes the name from the title that the attacker writes and turns each +, < and > of the title into a -, and each blank of the title into a - after trimming the blanks at the head and the end of the title, so that a + at the head of the title makes a - at the head of the name; the word is at a place in the order of the words of {command} where {command} reads a word that starts with - as an option, and the attacker can write at that place an option in the list {options}, which makes {command} run a program or code that is written after the name of the option
argument-injection.wiki.x-consequence: the attacker makes the attacker's value start with the name of one of the options that the finding names, followed by a program; the command reads the word as the option whose name starts the word, and runs the program in the step, with whatever the step can reach, such as the secrets and the token in its env, the credentials actions/checkout leaves in .git/config, the network, and sudo on a GitHub-hosted runner
argument-injection.wiki.x-remedy: A variable of env and double quotes ("$X") stop the shell from running the value as code, but the variable and the quotes do not stop the command from reading the value as an option. In either fix below, keep the value in the variable of env, and pass the variable to the command inside double quotes. Then either put the word that ends the command's options (--; --end-of-options for git) after the last option the command needs and before the value, for example right before the value (tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt -- "$X"), so that the command reads every word after that word as a plain argument; or, before the command, end the step with an error when the value starts with -, such as [[ $X != -* ]] || exit 1 for the variable X that holds the value. The shell check [[ $X != -* ]] works only when the command gets the value inside double quotes: when the command gets the value outside quotes, a blank in the value starts a new word, and the new word can start with -. For make, -- is not enough: make reads a word of the form NAME=value as the assignment of a variable even after --, so for make end the step with an error when the value starts with - or contains =, such as [[ $X != -* && $X != *=* ]] || exit 1

artifact-poisoning.download.description: A download of the artifact of a run an attacker drives into the workspace of a job that no one approves and that has the repository's secrets or a token that may write, where no step after the download is seen to run the files of the artifact: the harm holds when a step after the download runs the files of the artifact, which the fact download.executed answers.

uses.description: The uses of the download, as written.

pr_run_ref.description: What makes the download take the artifact of the attacker's run, as written: an expression such as github.event.workflow_run.id, the input allow_forks with the value true, or, when the step has no input run_id (or an input run_id whose ${{ }} is empty on the event of the job) and no input allow_forks with the value true, the value of the key uses of the step (dawidd6/action-download-artifact@<ref>), whose search of the runs of a workflow takes the attacker's run; or, for an artifact of the current run, jobs.<id> of the job that checks out the code of the pull request and uploads the artifact.

pr_code_on.description: The events on which the finding holds, each event named once.

artifact-poisoning.download.x-detected: {uses} takes the artifact of {pr_run_ref} into the workspace on {pr_code_on}
artifact-poisoning.download.x-consequence: its files replace those of the workspace; a step that runs any of them (a build, a test, a script) runs the pull request's author's code with the job's secrets and its token
artifact-poisoning.download.x-remedy: download to ${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts, or say in a file of facts that the files are only read as data

artifact-poisoning.executed.description: A download of the artifact of a run an attacker drives, in a job that no one approves and that has the repository's secrets or a token that may write, whose files a step after the download runs.

uses.description: The uses of the download, as written.

pr_run_ref.description: What makes the download take the artifact of the attacker's run, as written: an expression such as github.event.workflow_run.id, the input allow_forks with the value true, or, when the step has no input run_id (or an input run_id whose ${{ }} is empty on the event of the job) and no input allow_forks with the value true, the value of the key uses of the step (dawidd6/action-download-artifact@<ref>), whose search of the runs of a workflow takes the attacker's run; or, for an artifact of the current run, jobs.<id> of the job that checks out the code of the pull request and uploads the artifact.

pr_code_on.description: The events on which the finding holds, each event named once.

runs.description: The steps after the download that run the files of the artifact: for each step, the name of the step, or steps[<n>] when the step has no name, with n counted from 0 among all the steps of the job or of the action.

artifact-poisoning.executed.x-detected: {uses} takes the artifact of {pr_run_ref} on {pr_code_on}, and {runs} runs it
artifact-poisoning.executed.x-consequence: the author of a pull request from a fork makes the artifact, and runs their code with the job's secrets and its token
artifact-poisoning.executed.x-remedy: download to ${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts and read the files as data only, or run the pull request's code in the pull_request workflow and pass only data

artipacked.github-token.description: A step leaves the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in a file (.git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and an upload after the step puts that file in an artifact others can download while the job still runs.

uses.description: The uses of the step that leaves the token, as written.

upload.description: The uses, as written, of one upload that runs after the step and puts the file of the token in an artifact: the first of those uploads that puts the file in an artifact on no condition, else the first of those uploads.

artipacked.github-token.x-detected: {uses} leaves the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in a file (.git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and {upload} puts the file in an artifact while the job goes on
artipacked.github-token.x-consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the token and writes what the job may write until the job ends
artipacked.github-token.x-remedy: set persist-credentials: false on the checkout, or upload only the files the artifact needs

artipacked.token-input.description: A step leaves a token given to the step in a file (.git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and an upload after the step puts that file in an artifact.

uses.description: The uses of the step that leaves the token, as written.

upload.description: The uses, as written, of one upload that runs after the step and puts the file of the token in an artifact: the first of those uploads that puts the file in an artifact on no condition, else the first of those uploads.

artipacked.token-input.x-detected: {uses} leaves the token given to the step in a file (.git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and {upload} puts the file in an artifact
artipacked.token-input.x-consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the token, which does not expire when the job ends
artipacked.token-input.x-remedy: set persist-credentials: false on the checkout, or upload only the files the artifact needs

authored-command-name.description: A workflow command that GitHub deprecated (set-output, save-state) or disabled (set-env, add-path).

oneOf.description: set-output: sets an output of the step.
save-state: saves a value for the post step of the same action.
set-env: sets an environment variable of the later steps.
add-path: adds a directory to the PATH of the later steps.

bot-conditions.dependabot.description: A comparison of the actor in an if that a run of Dependabot passes: the attacker has Dependabot push to their pull request, and the actor is dependabot[bot].

path.description: The reference compared, as written, such as github.actor.

literal.description: The string or the number that the path is compared with.

attacker_on.description: The privileged events the if may run on, each event named once.

bot-conditions.dependabot.x-detected: {path} is compared with {literal} in an if on {attacker_on}, and a run of Dependabot's push to the attacker's pull request passes it
bot-conditions.dependabot.x-consequence: an attacker has the job run on their pull request: they comment @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's pull request in their fork, whose branch their pull request is from, and Dependabot's push makes the actor dependabot[bot]
bot-conditions.dependabot.x-remedy: compare the author of the pull request, github.event.pull_request.user.login, which Dependabot's push does not change

cache-bloat.partial-restore.description: A step that may save, under a new key, a cache restored from another key by restore-keys.

saves_on.description: The events on which the restore and the save both run and the save may save, each event named once.

cache-bloat.partial-restore.x-detected: the step may save under a new key the content of an older cache that restore-keys restored; the events on which the step may save: {saves_on}
cache-bloat.partial-restore.x-consequence: the content of the older caches stays in each new cache, so the new cache grows and takes longer to restore and to save; when the caches of the repository pass the cache limit, GitHub deletes the caches used least recently
cache-bloat.partial-restore.x-remedy: save the cache only in runs in which restore-keys restores no older cache (for example, a push run that builds without a restore), or remove restore-keys from the step

cache-poisoning.attacker-key.description: A step that saves to the cache of the default branch's scope under a key with a value an attacker writes, in a privileged job no one approves.

uses.description: The uses of the step, as written.

expression.description: The reference in the key, as written.

cache_write_on.description: The privileged events on which an attacker writes the value of the expression, each event named once.

cache-poisoning.attacker-key.x-detected: {uses} saves to the cache of the default branch's scope on {cache_write_on} under a key with {expression}, which an attacker writes
cache-poisoning.attacker-key.x-consequence: the attacker chooses the key, and saves first under one that later runs of the repository look up
cache-poisoning.attacker-key.x-remedy: make the key of values the attacker does not write, or make the cache-mode read or none

cache-poisoning.attacker-path.description: A step that saves to the cache of the default branch's scope a path with a value an attacker writes, in a privileged job no one approves.

uses.description: The uses of the step, as written.

expression.description: The reference in the path, as written.

cache_write_on.description: The privileged events on which an attacker writes the value of the expression, each event named once.

cache-poisoning.attacker-path.x-detected: {uses} saves to the cache of the default branch's scope on {cache_write_on} the path {expression}, which an attacker writes
cache-poisoning.attacker-path.x-consequence: the attacker chooses the files saved, such as the credential a checkout leaves in .git, and anyone who can open a pull request reads the caches of the default branch
cache-poisoning.attacker-path.x-remedy: make the path of values the attacker does not write, or make the cache-mode read or none

cache-poisoning.saved-checkout.description: A step that saves to the cache of the default branch's scope a path that has the code of a pull request a checkout brought, in a privileged job no one approves.

uses.description: The uses of the checkout, as written.

checkout_ref.description: The reference that names the pull request's code, as written.

save.description: The step that saves the path to the cache: the name of the step, or steps[<n>] when the step has no name, with n counted from 0 among all the steps of the job or of the action. For a step of a composite action that a step of the job runs, the name of the step, then of, then the uses of the composite action as written.

path.description: One line of the input path of the cache step (the input may have several lines), the line that names the checked out code, as written.

cache_write_on.description: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.

cache-poisoning.saved-checkout.x-detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {cache_write_on}, and {save} saves {path} to the cache of the default branch's scope
cache-poisoning.saved-checkout.x-consequence: the pull request's author puts their files in a cache that later runs of the repository restore and run, with no code of theirs run in the job
cache-poisoning.saved-checkout.x-remedy: check out the base's code, save to the cache only what the job builds from it, or make the cache-mode read or none

cache-poisoning.writable-job.description: A job that a privileged event runs and no one approves, whose cache-mode lets it save to the cache of the default branch's scope.

cache_mode.description: The cache-mode that lets the job save to the cache, as written.

cache_write_on.description: The privileged events on which the job may save to the cache, each event named once.

cache-poisoning.writable-job.x-detected: the job runs on {cache_write_on}, which an attacker triggers, with no approval, and cache-mode {cache_mode} lets it save to the cache of the default branch's scope
cache-poisoning.writable-job.x-consequence: a flaw that runs the attacker's code in the job, such as an injection or a checkout of their code, lets them save to the cache what later runs of the repository restore and run, a release among them
cache-poisoning.writable-job.x-remedy: make the cache-mode read or none, and save the cache from a workflow the attacker does not trigger, such as one on push

code-injection.controlled.description: A value an attacker controls, written into a script by ${{ }}.

expr_ref.description: The reference in the expression, such as github.event.issue.title.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the expression, each event named once.

code-injection.controlled.x-detected: {expr_ref} is written into {sink_kind} by ${{ }}, and an attacker controls it on {controlled_on}
code-injection.controlled.x-remedy: pass it through env and read the variable

code-injection.env-variable.description: A variable of env whose value an attacker controls, which a run of bash reads as code.

variable.description: The variable, written as in the run, such as $ISSUE_TITLE, or the bare name of a variable in an arithmetic expression, such as TITLE in $(( TITLE + 1 )).

expr_ref.description: The reference that an attacker controls in the value of env, such as github.event.issue.title, or the value of the github context that the runner writes into the variable, such as github.head_ref for GITHUB_HEAD_REF.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the variable, each event named once.

code-injection.env-variable.x-detected: the script of the step (run:) passes the value of the variable {variable} to {code_reading}, and the value of the variable comes from {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on {controlled_on}
code-injection.env-variable.x-remedy: do not pass the variable to eval (eval "..."), to the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c (bash -c "...", python3 -c "..."), to the command name at the start of a command ($VAR arg), to the input of a shell (| bash) or to arithmetic ($(( ... )), [[ ... -eq ... ]]); pass the variable only as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data, such as printf '%s\n' "$VAR". Keep the variable inside double quotes there: without the quotes the value stays data, but bash splits the value into words and expands * and ?

code-injection.env-variable-wiki.description: A variable of env whose value is controlled on gollum alone, which a run of bash reads as code: it holds if anyone may edit the wiki.

variable.description: The variable, written as in the run.

expr_ref.description: The reference that an attacker controls in the value of env.

code-injection.env-variable-wiki.x-detected: the script of the step (run:) passes the value of the variable {variable} to {code_reading}, and the value of the variable comes from {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on gollum
code-injection.env-variable-wiki.x-remedy: do not pass the variable to eval (eval "..."), to the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c (bash -c "...", python3 -c "..."), to the command name at the start of a command ($VAR arg), to the input of a shell (| bash) or to arithmetic ($(( ... )), [[ ... -eq ... ]]); pass the variable only as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data, such as printf '%s\n' "$VAR". Keep the variable inside double quotes there: without the quotes the value stays data, but bash splits the value into words and expands * and ?

code-injection.wiki.description: A value controlled on gollum alone, written into a script by ${{ }}: it holds if anyone may edit the wiki.

expr_ref.description: The reference in the expression.

code-injection.wiki.x-detected: {expr_ref} is written into {sink_kind} by ${{ }}, and an attacker controls it on gollum
code-injection.wiki.x-remedy: pass it through env and read the variable

code-reading.description: How bash, or a program that bash gives the value to, reads the value of a variable as code.

oneOf.description: An argument that the command reads as code: an operand of eval (eval "..."), the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c (bash -c "...", python3 -c "..."), or a program that git runs (git -c core.fsmonitor="...").

A variable outside quotes as the command name at the start of a command ($VAR arg): bash splits the value into words, and the first word names the program that runs, with the other words as its arguments.
The input of a command that runs the input as code: the body of a heredoc whose delimiter is not quoted, a here-string, or what echo, printf or cat writes right before a pipe (echo "$VAR" | bash).

An arithmetic expression ($(( ... )), (( ... )), [[ ... -eq ... ]], an array subscript), or the name that read, printf -v or test -v takes: bash evaluates the value as arithmetic, and a value such as a[$(...)] holds an array subscript whose command substitution runs.
The transformation ${VAR@P}: bash expands the value of the variable as a prompt string, and runs a command substitution such as $(...) in the value.

x-text.code-argument: a command that reads the value as code (eval "...", the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c, such as bash -c "..." or python3 -c "...", git -c core.fsmonitor="...")
x-text.command-word: the command name at the start of a command, outside quotes ($VAR arg), where bash splits the value into words and the first word names the program that runs
x-text.code-input: a command that runs its input as code (echo "$VAR" | bash, bash <<< "$VAR")
x-text.arithmetic: arithmetic ($(( ... )), (( ... )), [[ ... -eq ... ]]), where a value such as a[$(...)] holds an array subscript whose command substitution runs
x-text.prompt-expansion: the transformation ${VAR@P}, which expands the value of the variable as a prompt string and runs a command substitution such as $(...) in the value

commit-sha.unpinned.description: A remote uses whose ref is not a full commit SHA.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

repo.description: The repository, owner/name as written; not always a name GitHub can have.

commit-sha.unpinned.x-detected: {uses} is not pinned to a full commit SHA
commit-sha.unpinned.x-consequence: whoever can move the ref decides what runs here
commit-sha.unpinned.x-remedy: pin the uses to a full commit SHA

commit-sha.unpinned-path-action.description: A uses of another repository whose path goes with .. above the root of the repository and names, in the directory where the runner puts the actions of the job, an action whose ref is not a full commit SHA.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

action.description: The action that runs, as owner/repo@ref: the repository and the ref that the path names after the .., read from _actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref> on the runner.

commit-sha.unpinned-path-action.x-detected: the path of {uses} goes with .. above the root of the repository and runs {action}, so the ref after @ does not decide the code that runs; {action} is not pinned to a full commit SHA
commit-sha.unpinned-path-action.x-consequence: whoever can move the ref of the action that runs decides what runs here
commit-sha.unpinned-path-action.x-remedy: write a uses of the action that runs, as owner/repo/path@ref without .., and pin that uses to a full commit SHA

cond.mixed-text.description: An if that GitHub reads as a string: text outside its ${{ }}, or more than one ${{ }}.

condition.description: The value of the if, as written.

status_functions.description: The status functions that an expression in a ${{ }} of the if calls, once each; empty when the if calls none.

cond.mixed-text.x-detected: the if {condition} has text outside its ${{ }} (in an action.yml, a space or a line break counts as text too), or more than one ${{ }}, so GitHub reads the if as a string
cond.mixed-text.x-consequence: GitHub joins the text and the values of the expressions into one string; the string is not empty, so the string is true whatever the expressions give. When no ${{ }} of the if calls a status function (always(), cancelled(), failure() or success()), GitHub adds success() && before the string, and the job or the step runs only when the jobs or the steps before the job or the step succeeded. When a ${{ }} calls a status function, even success(), GitHub adds nothing, the if is the string alone, and the job or the step runs after a failure too. When the if is written to keep an attacker from running the job or the step, the if does not stop the attacker: the rules of this linter that evaluate the if in the runs of an attacker read the if as true, as GitHub does, and read the job or the step as when the job or the step has no if: for example, dangerous-triggers reports a job that runs on an event of the attacker with secrets or a token that writes. What the attacker gets comes from what the job or the step does, not from the if alone
cond.mixed-text.x-remedy: write the whole condition in one ${{ }}, such as ${{ a && b }}, or write the condition without ${{ }}, such as a && b; both forms work in a workflow and in an action.yml. In an action.yml, write nothing around the ${{ }}: no space, and no block scalar (if: |), which keeps a line break after the ${{ }}

credentials.private.description: The password of a registry written in the workflow of a private repository.
credentials.private.x-detected: the password of {container} is written in the workflow
credentials.private.x-consequence: whoever reads the repository reads it, and its history keeps it if the repository is made public
credentials.private.x-remedy: revoke the password, and pass a new one from a secret of the repository

credentials.public.description: The password of a registry written in the workflow of a public repository.
credentials.public.x-detected: the password of {container} is written in the workflow
credentials.public.x-consequence: anyone reads it in a public repository, and its history keeps it
credentials.public.x-remedy: revoke the password, and pass a new one from a secret of the repository

dangerous-triggers.secrets.description: A job that a privileged event runs and no one approves, which reads secrets.

privileged_on.description: The privileged events that the job can run on, each event named once.

secrets.description: The names of the secrets that the job reads; for a job that calls a reusable workflow, the names of the secrets that GitHub passes to the runners of the jobs of the called workflow. The single value * when the job, or a job of the reusable workflow that the job calls with secrets: inherit, reads the secrets without naming the secrets, or when the job calls with secrets: inherit a reusable workflow whose contents the linter does not have. For a job that passes secrets one by one to a reusable workflow whose contents the linter does not have, every passed secret.

dangerous-triggers.secrets.x-detected: the job runs on {privileged_on}, which an attacker triggers, with no approval, and reads the secrets {secrets}
dangerous-triggers.secrets.x-consequence: a flaw that runs the attacker's code in the job, such as an injection or a checkout of their code, gives them the secrets and what they open past the repository
dangerous-triggers.secrets.x-remedy: move the secrets to a job that the attacker's events do not run, or have a person approve it with an environment that has required reviewers

dangerous-triggers.token-write.description: A job that a privileged event runs and no one approves, whose GITHUB_TOKEN may write.

privileged_on.description: The privileged events that the job can run on, each event named once.

dangerous-triggers.token-write.x-detected: the job runs on {privileged_on}, which an attacker triggers, with no approval and a GITHUB_TOKEN that may write
dangerous-triggers.token-write.x-consequence: a flaw that runs the attacker's code in the job, such as an injection or a checkout of their code, gives them a token that pushes, releases and writes what the job may
dangerous-triggers.token-write.x-remedy: write permissions on the job with only the scopes it needs, or have a person approve it with an environment that has required reviewers

dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool.description: A file whose uses no update tool updates: no entry of Dependabot version updates reads the file, and Renovate does not update the file.

uses.description: The first uses of the file that no update tool updates, as written.

directory.description: The directory that an entry of .github/dependabot.yml would have to list for Dependabot to read the file: / for a workflow right under .github/workflows and for the action.yml or action.yaml at the root of the repository (Dependabot reads those files for the directory /); else the directory of the file from the root, starting with /, such as /.github/actions/build.

dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool.x-detected: no update tool updates {uses} and every other such uses of the same file, if there are any: no entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions lists {directory}, the directory that an entry would have to list for Dependabot to read the file, with version updates enabled (an entry whose open-pull-requests-limit is 0 does not count), and no Renovate configuration in the repository updates the file
dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool.x-consequence: when a new version of an action or a reusable workflow is released, no pull request updates the uses; a uses pinned to a commit SHA never gets a Dependabot alert or a security update, whatever the configuration, so version updates are the only updates of such a uses, and without them the workflow keeps running the old commit until a person changes the uses
dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool.x-remedy: create .github/dependabot.yml with version: 2 if the repository has none, and add to the updates of .github/dependabot.yml an entry with package-ecosystem: github-actions whose key directory: or key directories: lists the directory named in the finding; or configure Renovate to update the file

dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sh.description: A file whose uses pinned to a commit SHA without a version comment Renovate does not update, and that no entry of Dependabot version updates reads.

uses.description: The first uses of the file that is pinned to a commit SHA without a version comment, as written.

directory.description: The directory that an entry of .github/dependabot.yml would have to list for Dependabot to read the file: / for a workflow right under .github/workflows and for the action.yml or action.yaml at the root of the repository (Dependabot reads those files for the directory /); else the directory of the file from the root, starting with /, such as /.github/actions/build.

dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sh.x-detected: Renovate updates the file, but does not update {uses} and every other uses of the same file that is pinned to a commit SHA without a version comment, if there are any; and no entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions lists {directory}, the directory that an entry would have to list for Dependabot to read the file, with version updates enabled (an entry whose open-pull-requests-limit is 0 does not count)
dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sh.x-consequence: Renovate skips a uses pinned to a commit SHA when the line of the uses has no comment that names a version; a uses pinned to a commit SHA never gets a Dependabot alert or a security update, whatever the configuration, so when a new version is released, no pull request updates the uses, and the workflow keeps running the old commit until a person changes the uses
dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sh.x-remedy: write the version of the commit as a comment at the end of the line of each such uses, such as # v4.1.0, so that Renovate updates the uses; or create .github/dependabot.yml with version: 2 if the repository has none, and add to the updates of .github/dependabot.yml an entry with package-ecosystem: github-actions whose key directory: or key directories: lists the directory named in the finding

dependency-review-settings.comment-witho.description: A step of actions/dependency-review-action that asks for a comment on the pull request in a job whose GITHUB_TOKEN is not given pull-requests: write.
dependency-review-settings.comment-witho.x-detected: the step asks to write the summary of the dependency review as a comment on the pull request, but the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job is not given pull-requests: write
dependency-review-settings.comment-witho.x-consequence: the comment is not written: the step warns and succeeds
dependency-review-settings.comment-witho.x-remedy: give the job pull-requests: write, or set comment-summary-in-pr to never

dependency-review-settings.license-polic.description: A step of actions/dependency-review-action with license-check false and a license policy written.
dependency-review-settings.license-polic.x-detected: license-check is false, so the license policy written is not checked
dependency-review-settings.license-polic.x-consequence: dependencies with a denied license, or with a license that is not in the allowed list, pass the review
dependency-review-settings.license-polic.x-remedy: remove license-check: false, or remove the license policy

dependency-review-settings.vulnerability.description: A step of actions/dependency-review-action with vulnerability-check false.
dependency-review-settings.vulnerability.x-consequence: dependencies with known vulnerabilities pass the review

dependency-review-settings.warn-only.description: A step of actions/dependency-review-action with warn-only true.
dependency-review-settings.warn-only.x-consequence: vulnerabilities and license violations only warn: the step succeeds, and a required check does not stop the pull request
dependency-review-settings.warn-only.x-remedy: remove warn-only: true; fail-on-severity sets the lowest severity that fails the step

deprecated-commands.deprecated-command.description: A workflow command set-output or save-state that the run script of a step, in bash or sh, prints to the log of the step as ::name at the head of a line or ##[name anywhere in a line, with the name of the command in the text of the run script.
deprecated-commands.deprecated-command.x-detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command {command}, which GitHub deprecated
deprecated-commands.deprecated-command.x-consequence: the runner adds a warning to each run of the workflow that runs the step. GitHub planned to disable both commands on 2023-05-31, and the notice of 2023-07-24 postponed the date without a new date. For set-output: once GitHub disables set-output, the step sets no output. For save-state: only the post step of the same action reads the state, and a run script has no post step, so no step reads the state that a run script saves
deprecated-commands.deprecated-command.x-remedy: for set-output, write name=value to the file $GITHUB_OUTPUT; for a value of many lines, write the line name<<DELIM, the lines of the value and the line DELIM, where DELIM is a random text that the value does not contain. For save-state, remove the command, because no step reads the state that a run script saves

deprecated-commands.disabled-command.description: A workflow command set-env or add-path that the run script of a step, in bash or sh, prints to the log of the step as ::name at the head of a line or ##[name anywhere in a line, with the name of the command in the text of the run script.
deprecated-commands.disabled-command.x-detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command {command}, which GitHub disabled
deprecated-commands.disabled-command.x-consequence: when ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is not true for the step, the runner fails the step. When ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true, the command works, and each line that the step prints as a set-env or add-path command sets the environment variables or the PATH of the later steps; a value of an attacker that such a step prints is reported by the rule unsecure-commands
deprecated-commands.disabled-command.x-remedy: write name=value to the file $GITHUB_ENV for set-env, or the directory to the file $GITHUB_PATH for add-path, and remove ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS

deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime.description: An action.yml whose runs.using is node12, node16 or node20.
deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime.x-detected: the action declares runs.using: {runs_using}, an older Node.js version than node24
deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime.x-consequence: GitHub-hosted runners run the action on Node.js 24 (seen on 2026-10-20), not on the Node.js version that the action declares, and add a warning to every run of every job that uses the action; code of the action that depends on the declared Node.js version may behave differently on Node.js 24

For the secrets that a job gives a called workflow, the jobs of the called workflow fail before their first steps run. For the outputs and environment.url of a job, that job fails after the steps of that job ran. For the value of an output of workflow_call, the jobs of the called workflow succeed, and the jobs that need the job that calls the workflow do not run
