secrets.description: What the request carries: the names of the secrets as written, GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token, * for the whole secrets context, or enterprise-token for the token gh api reads from GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN or GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN when no secret is known to be in that variable.

expr_ref.description: The reference whose value decides the host, such as github.event.issue.title.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker controls the value, each event named once.

request-forgery.action-input.x-detected: {action} sends {secrets} to the server that its input {input} names, and the input {input} has the value of {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on the events {controlled_on}
request-forgery.action-input.x-consequence: the attacker writes the address of a server of the attacker's own into the value: in args of SonarSource's scanner, one more argument -Dsonar.host.url=<the server>; in route or url of octokit/request-action, a full URL; the action sends the credential to that server, and the attacker uses the credential as the job would
request-forgery.action-input.x-remedy: keep a value an attacker controls out of the input: in args of SonarSource's scanner, pass only values written literally in the workflow file; in route or url of octokit/request-action, write the host in the workflow and put the attacker's value only in the path after the host, or in a parameter of the request

request-forgery.credential-host.description: A value an attacker controls decides the host of a request that a command of a run sends, and the request carries a secret or the job's token.

command.description: The command that sends the request: curl, wget or gh api.

secrets.description: What the request carries: the names of the secrets as written, GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token, * for the whole secrets context, or enterprise-token for the token gh api reads from GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN or GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN when no secret is known to be in that variable.

expr_ref.description: The reference whose value decides the host, such as github.event.issue.title.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker controls the value, each event named once.

request-forgery.credential-host.x-detected: {command} sends a request whose host the value of {expr_ref} decides, and an attacker controls the value on the events {controlled_on}; the request carries {secrets}
request-forgery.credential-host.x-consequence: the attacker writes the host of a server of the attacker's own into the value; the command sends the request, with each secret the request carries, to that server, and the attacker uses each secret as the job would: reading what the secret gives access to, and, when the request carries the job's token (GITHUB_TOKEN) and the token can write, writing to the repository while the job runs
request-forgery.credential-host.x-remedy: do not let a value an attacker controls decide the host of a request that carries a credential: write the host in the workflow and put the attacker's value only after the / that ends the host (https://api.example.com/<the value>). A check in the script that ends the step with an error when the value is not one of the hosts the workflow expects also stops the attack, but the linter does not read such a check and keeps reporting the request

request-forgery.runner-network.description: A value an attacker controls decides the host of a request from a job on a self-hosted runner: the request reaches the network of the runner, which the attacker does not reach.

command.description: What sends the request: the command curl, wget or gh api, or an action and the input of the action, such as octokit/request-action route.

runner_labels.description: The labels of the job's runs-on, as written.

expr_ref.description: The reference whose value decides the host, such as github.event.issue.title.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker controls the value, each event named once.

request-forgery.runner-network.x-detected: {command} sends a request whose host the value of {expr_ref} decides, and an attacker controls the value on the events {controlled_on}; the job runs on a self-hosted runner ({runner_labels})
request-forgery.runner-network.x-consequence: the attacker writes the address of a service of the runner's network into the value, such as a service of an internal network or a cloud's metadata service; the request reaches that service from the runner, although the attacker cannot reach that service from outside, and the attacker can make the service act or, where the response comes back to the attacker, read the response
request-forgery.runner-network.x-remedy: either write the host of the request in the workflow, so that a value an attacker controls does not decide the host, or run the job on a GitHub-hosted runner, which does not reach the network of the self-hosted runner, when the job does not need that network; either one alone removes the finding. A check in the script that ends the step with an error when the value is not one of the hosts the workflow expects also stops the attack, but the linter does not read such a check and keeps reporting the request

secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destinatio.description: A request that a command of a run sends carries a secret or the job's token to a destination the workflow names, and no file of facts says to trust that destination with that secret (request.destination-trusted).

command.description: The command that sends the request: curl, wget or gh api.

secret.description: The name of the secret the request carries, as the fact names the secret: in upper case, GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token.

destination.description: Where the request goes, as the fact names the destination: the host, or the origin of the value that names the host, such as ${{ secrets.UPLOAD_API }}.

secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destinatio.x-detected: {command} sends {secret} to {destination}, and no file of facts says to trust {destination} with {secret}
secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destinatio.x-consequence: whoever runs the server of the destination, or takes the server over (a breached vendor, or whoever registers a lapsed domain), receives the secret or the job's token and can use the secret or the token as the job would
secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destinatio.x-remedy: if the destination is the service that the secret is for, answer true for the pair of the secret (GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token) and the destination, with --fact 'request.destination-trusted[secret=API_KEY,destination=api.example.com]=true' or the same query in a file of facts given with --facts; if the destination is not, remove the secret from the request

secret-exposure.all-secrets.description: A reference in a ${{ }} that reads the secrets context and names no secret: toJSON(secrets), secrets[x] whose x is not a string literal, secrets.*.
secret-exposure.all-secrets.x-detected: {reference} reads the secrets without naming one
secret-exposure.all-secrets.x-consequence: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository, including the secrets that no expression of the job names, and also every secret of the environment of the job when the job references an environment. The memory of the runner holds every secret that GitHub sends the job, and code that runs in a step of the job can read every secret in the memory of the runner. The harm comes from two kinds of code: an action that turns malicious, and code that an attacker writes and that a flaw of the job runs. The harm is each secret that one of the two kinds of code can read now and could not read if each job of each workflow that can read the secret named only the secrets that the job needs. In the workflows that name only the needed secrets, GitHub sends each job only the secrets that the job names, and code that runs in a job can still read every secret that the job names. An action counts in every job, of any workflow, that runs the action; the code of an attacker counts only in the jobs whose flaw runs the code of the attacker
secret-exposure.all-secrets.x-remedy: name each secret the job needs, secrets.NAME, and pick one by an if for each value of the matrix rather than by a secrets[...] whose name is computed

secret-in-log.private.description: A value the shell made from a secret, which the runner does not mask, printed to the log of a run in a private repository.

secret.description: The name of the secret, in upper case; GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token.

transform.description: How the shell made the value from the secret: the operator of a parameter expansion (substring, prefix-removal, suffix-removal, replacement, case-change, expansion), or the command (jq, base64 and the like).

secret-in-log.private.x-detected: {transform} makes a value from the secret {secret}, and the value is printed in {place}
secret-in-log.private.x-consequence: the runner registers the secret, each line of the secret and encoded forms of the secret such as the base64 of the secret, and masks only those strings, not a value the shell makes from the secret: whoever has read access to the repository reads the value in the log; the log of the run is kept for 90 days by default
secret-in-log.private.x-remedy: do not print the value; if the value must be printed, register each line of the value with ::add-mask:: before the value is printed; delete the logs of the runs that printed the value, and rotate the secret

secret-in-log.public.description: A value the shell made from a secret, which the runner does not mask, printed to the log of a run in a public repository.

secret.description: The name of the secret, in upper case; GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token.

transform.description: How the shell made the value from the secret: the operator of a parameter expansion (substring, prefix-removal, suffix-removal, replacement, case-change, expansion), or the command (jq, base64 and the like).

secret-in-log.public.x-detected: {transform} makes a value from the secret {secret}, and the value is printed in {place}
secret-in-log.public.x-consequence: the runner registers the secret, each line of the secret and encoded forms of the secret such as the base64 of the secret, and masks only those strings, not a value the shell makes from the secret: anyone signed in to GitHub reads the value in the log; the log of the run is kept for 90 days by default
secret-in-log.public.x-remedy: do not print the value; if the value must be printed, register each line of the value with ::add-mask:: before the value is printed; delete the logs of the runs that printed the value, and rotate the secret

secrets-in-artifacts.job-scoped.description: A step leaves a credential that works while the job runs in a file of the workspace, and an upload after it puts the file in an artifact others can download while the job still runs.

uses.description: The uses, as written, of one step that runs before the upload and leaves a credential that the upload takes: the first of those steps that leaves a credential on no condition, else the first of those steps.

upload.description: The uses of the upload, as written.

secrets-in-artifacts.job-scoped.x-detected: {uses} leaves a credential that works while the job runs in the workspace, and {upload} puts it in an artifact while the job goes on
secrets-in-artifacts.job-scoped.x-consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the credential and uses what it opens until the job ends
secrets-in-artifacts.job-scoped.x-remedy: leave the file out of the path (a line !gha-creds-*.json), or upload before the step that writes it

secrets-in-artifacts.lasting.description: A step leaves a credential that does not expire with the job in a file of the workspace, and an upload after it puts the file in an artifact.

uses.description: The uses, as written, of one step that runs before the upload and leaves a credential that the upload takes: the first of those steps that leaves a credential on no condition, else the first of those steps.

upload.description: The uses of the upload, as written.

secrets-in-artifacts.lasting.x-detected: {uses} leaves a credential that does not expire in the workspace, and {upload} puts it in an artifact
secrets-in-artifacts.lasting.x-consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the credential and uses what it opens
secrets-in-artifacts.lasting.x-remedy: leave the file out of the path (a line !gha-creds-*.json), upload before the step that writes it, or have the step not write it (create_credentials_file: false)

secrets-inherit.local.description: A job that calls a reusable workflow of the same repository with secrets: inherit, which lets the called workflow reference every secret; reported when either a job of the called workflow reads the secrets without naming the secrets, or the linter does not have the contents of the called workflow.

uses.description: The uses of the job, as written.

secrets-inherit.local.x-detected: the job calls {uses} with secrets: inherit, and either a job of the called workflow reads the secrets without naming the secrets (toJSON(secrets), secrets[<an expression>], secrets.*), or the linter does not have the contents of the called workflow
secrets-inherit.local.x-consequence: GitHub passes every secret of the organization and the repository that the job has to the runner of a job of the called workflow that reads the secrets without naming the secrets; a flaw that runs an attacker's code in that job, such as an injection, gives the attacker every one of those secrets, not only the secrets that the called workflow needs
secrets-inherit.local.x-remedy: in the called workflow, read each secret by name in place of toJSON(secrets), secrets[<an expression>] or secrets.*; or declare in on.workflow_call.secrets of the called workflow the secrets that the called workflow reads, and pass those secrets one by one under secrets:

secrets-inherit.remote.description: A job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository with secrets: inherit, which lets the called workflow reference every secret.

uses.description: The uses of the job, as written.

secrets-inherit.remote.x-detected: the job calls {uses}, a reusable workflow of another repository, with secrets: inherit, which lets the called workflow reference every secret that the job has
secrets-inherit.remote.x-consequence: whoever maintains that repository, or takes it over, reads every secret of the organization and the repository, not only those the workflow needs
secrets-inherit.remote.x-remedy: declare in on.workflow_call.secrets of the called workflow the secrets it reads, and pass those one by one under secrets:

self-hosted-runner.private.description: A job of a private or internal repository, whose readers may fork it and whose pull requests from forks run their workflows, that runs on a self-hosted runner.

label.description: The label that names the self-hosted runner, as written or as the matrix gives the label.

self-hosted-runner.private.x-detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner ({label}) of a private or internal repository that runs the workflows of pull requests from its forks
self-hosted-runner.private.x-consequence: one who may read the repository and fork it, which every member of the enterprise reads for an internal one, can open a pull request that runs their code on the runner, whose state persists for the jobs after it: their secrets, their tokens and the runner's network
self-hosted-runner.private.x-remedy: turn off Run workflows from fork pull requests, which the rule reads as the fact repo.fork-pr-run-workflows (with the fact false, the rule reports nothing), or run the jobs on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. On self-hosted runners that no pull request from a fork reaches, the rule still reports the job, as the rule reads the labels of runs-on only. An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.

self-hosted-runner.public.description: A job of a public repository that runs on a self-hosted runner.

label.description: The label that names the self-hosted runner, as written or as the matrix gives the label.

self-hosted-runner.public.x-detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner ({label}) of a public repository
self-hosted-runner.public.x-consequence: anyone who opens a pull request can run their code on the runner, whose state persists for the jobs after it: their secrets, their tokens and the runner's network
self-hosted-runner.public.x-remedy: run the jobs of a public repository on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. An owner of the organization can instead put the self-hosted runners in a runner group that does not allow public repositories: no job of the repository reaches those runners, though the rule still reports the job, as the rule reads the labels of runs-on only (the false positive form group-access). An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.

set-output-injection.controlled.description: A value an attacker controls, printed to the log of a step that has an id.

expr_ref.description: The reference as written: a context in ${{ }}, such as github.event.issue.title, or a variable of env, such as $TITLE.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker writes a workflow command in the value, each event named once.

set-output-injection.controlled.x-detected: the value of {expr_ref} is printed to the log of a step, the step has an id, and an attacker who controls the value on {controlled_on} can write a set-output command in the value
set-output-injection.controlled.x-consequence: with or without ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS, the runner reads a line that the step prints, when the line holds ##[set-output name=NAME;]value or starts with ::set-output, as a command that sets the output NAME of the step; the runner sets the outputs of a step only when the step has an id; the steps after the step, and the outputs of the job and of an action that name the output, get the value of the attacker as the output of the step, and a step that writes ${{ steps.<id>.outputs.NAME }} into its run script runs code of the attacker
set-output-injection.controlled.x-remedy: do not print the value to the log; if the value must be printed, print the value only between ::stop-commands::TOKEN and ::TOKEN::, where TOKEN is a value the step chooses at random for each run (the rule does not read stop-commands and keeps reporting the step: a known false positive, stopped-commands)

sink-kind.description: The kind of script in which a value is written as code: the run script of a step, or the script of actions/github-script.

oneOf.description: The run script of a step.

status-function.description: A function an if may call that reads the status of the jobs or the steps before.

unmasked-secret-exposure.private.description: A ${{ }} whose value has a value taken out of a secret by fromJSON, where the runner prints it in the log, in a private repository.

secrets.description: The names of the secrets that the value is taken out of; * for a secret not named.

unmasked-secret-exposure.private.x-detected: a value taken out of the secrets {secrets} is written where the runner prints it
unmasked-secret-exposure.private.x-consequence: the runner masks only whole secrets, and a value taken out of a secret is not a whole secret. When a step has such a value in its env, with or run, the runner prints the value unmasked in the header of the step, before the step runs. When a container has such a value in its env, or in the username of its credentials, the runner prints the value unmasked in the docker commands that the runner prints at the start of the job, before any step runs. Whoever has read access to the repository reads the value in the log, which is kept for 90 days by default
unmasked-secret-exposure.private.x-remedy: store each value in a secret of its own, secrets.NAME; delete the logs that have it and rotate it

unmasked-secret-exposure.public.description: A ${{ }} whose value has a value taken out of a secret by fromJSON, where the runner prints it in the log, in a public repository.

secrets.description: The names of the secrets that the value is taken out of; * for a secret not named.

unmasked-secret-exposure.public.x-detected: a value taken out of the secrets {secrets} is written where the runner prints it
unmasked-secret-exposure.public.x-consequence: the runner masks only whole secrets, and a value taken out of a secret is not a whole secret. When a step has such a value in its env, with or run, the runner prints the value unmasked in the header of the step, before the step runs. When a container has such a value in its env, or in the username of its credentials, the runner prints the value unmasked in the docker commands that the runner prints at the start of the job, before any step runs. Anyone signed in to GitHub reads the value in the log, which is kept for 90 days by default

unpinned-images.mutable.description: An image that the steps of a job run in (a job's container, a step's docker://, an action's runs.image), which no digest pins.

image.description: The image as written, without docker://, or as the matrix gives the image.

tag.description: The tag of the image; empty when the image has no tag, which means the tag latest.

unpinned-images.mutable.x-detected: {image} of {site} is not pinned by a digest
unpinned-images.mutable.x-consequence: whoever can push the image's tag decides what the steps run in, with their secrets and token; no tag or latest, and a tag of a version series, also move on normal releases, unreviewed
unpinned-images.mutable.x-remedy: pin the image by its digest, as name@sha256:…

unpinned-images.service.description: The image of a service of a job, which no digest pins.

image.description: The image as written, or as the matrix gives the image.

tag.description: The tag of the image; empty when the image has no tag, which means the tag latest.

unpinned-images.service.x-detected: {image} of the service {service} is not pinned by a digest
unpinned-images.service.x-consequence: whoever can push the image's tag decides what runs beside the job: it reads the service's env and what the job sends it, and answers the job; no tag or latest, and a tag of a version series, also move on normal releases, unreviewed
unpinned-images.service.x-remedy: pin the image by its digest, as name@sha256:…

unsecure-commands.controlled.description: A value an attacker controls, printed to the log of a step where ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true.

expr_ref.description: The reference as written: a context in ${{ }}, such as github.event.issue.title, or a variable of env, such as $TITLE.

controlled_on.description: The events on which an attacker writes a workflow command in the value, each event named once.

unsecure-commands.controlled.x-detected: the value of {expr_ref} is printed to the log of a step where ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true, as set in {flag}, and an attacker who controls the value on {controlled_on} can write a set-env or add-path command in the value
unsecure-commands.controlled.x-consequence: the runner reads a line of the output that holds ##[set-env name=NAME;]value, or starts with ::set-env, as a command that sets the environment variable NAME of the steps after the step; a set-env of BASH_ENV makes the bash of each step after the step run code of the attacker, and an add-path puts a directory of the attacker before the PATH of the steps after the step
unsecure-commands.controlled.x-remedy: rewrite the steps that print set-env or add-path commands to write $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_PATH instead, then remove ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS; if the flag must stay, print values an attacker controls only between ::stop-commands::TOKEN and ::TOKEN::, where TOKEN is a value the step chooses at random for each run (the rule does not read stop-commands and keeps reporting the step)

unsecure-commands.wiki.description: A value an attacker controls on gollum alone, printed to the log of a step where ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true: the finding holds if anyone may edit the wiki.

expr_ref.description: The reference as written: a context in ${{ }}, such as github.event.issue.title, or a variable of env, such as $TITLE.

unsecure-commands.wiki.x-detected: the value of {expr_ref} is printed to the log of a step where ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true, as set in {flag}, and an attacker who controls the value on gollum alone can make the value hold an add-path command; for the name of a wiki page (page_name), the attacker does so through the title of the page: GitHub makes the name of the page from the title that the attacker writes, turns each blank of the title into a - after trimming the blanks at the head and the end of the title, and turns each - that the attacker writes in the title into the character U+2010, so that the attacker writes a blank where the command needs a -: the title ::add path::DIR makes the name ::add-path::DIR, and the title ##[add path]DIR makes the name ##[add-path]DIR
unsecure-commands.wiki.x-consequence: the runner reads a line of the output that holds ##[add-path]DIR anywhere in the line, or that starts with ::add-path::DIR, as a command that puts the directory DIR before the PATH of the steps after the step, so that an executable of the attacker in DIR runs in place of the program that a step after the step calls by name; the title ##[add path]DIR of a wiki page makes the name ##[add-path]DIR, and the title ::add path::DIR makes the name ::add-path::DIR
unsecure-commands.wiki.x-remedy: rewrite the steps that print set-env or add-path commands to write $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_PATH instead, then remove ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS; if the flag must stay, print values an attacker controls only between ::stop-commands::TOKEN and ::TOKEN::, where TOKEN is a value the step chooses at random for each run (the rule does not read stop-commands and keeps reporting the step)

unset-configuration-variable.empty-value.description: A reference to a configuration variable whose name no level defines, where the empty string becomes the value of the ${{ }}.

name.description: The name of the configuration variable, as written.

unset-configuration-variable.empty-value.x-detected: the expression {expression} reads the configuration variable {name} as a value, and no list of defined names that this run of the linter has (repo.configuration-variables, and repo.environment-configuration-variables of each environment whose configuration variables the place of the expression reads) has the name {name}
unset-configuration-variable.empty-value.x-consequence: GitHub gives the empty string for a configuration variable that no level (repository, organization, environment) defines, and GitHub reports no error, so the expression gives the empty string where the workflow expects the value of the configuration variable. A misspelled name shows only in what the workflow run does, such as an empty argument of a step
unset-configuration-variable.empty-value.x-remedy: define the configuration variable at the repository, organization or environment level, or correct the name in the expression; when the workflow reads a missing configuration variable on purpose as meaning that the setting is not given, write the default value after ||, such as vars.NAME || 'default'

unset-configuration-variable.failed-from.description: A reference to a configuration variable whose name no level defines, as the argument of fromJSON().

name.description: The name of the configuration variable, as written.

unset-configuration-variable.failed-from.x-detected: the expression {expression} gives the configuration variable {name} to fromJSON(), and no list of defined names that this run of the linter has (repo.configuration-variables, and repo.environment-configuration-variables of each environment whose configuration variables the place of the expression reads) has the name {name}

unset-configuration-variable.failed-from.x-remedy: define the configuration variable with a JSON value, or correct the name in the expression; when the workflow reads a missing configuration variable on purpose, give fromJSON() a JSON value for the missing case, such as fromJSON(vars.NAME || '[]')

unsound-contains.substring.description: A call of contains, startsWith or endsWith of a string in an if that a part of the string passes, where comparing whole values would keep the attacker out.

attacker_on.description: The privileged events the if may run on, each event named once.

unsound-contains.substring.x-detected: {func} of '{literal}' and {path} in an if on {attacker_on} lets a part of the string through
unsound-contains.substring.x-consequence: an attacker passes the if with a value that is only a part of one in the string, such as a login that is part of a name
unsound-contains.substring.x-remedy: compare whole values: contains(fromJSON('[...]'), the reference)

unsound-contains.superstring.description: A call of contains, startsWith or endsWith of a reference and a string in an if that a value with the string as a part passes, where comparing the whole value would keep the attacker out.

attacker_on.description: The privileged events the if may run on, each event named once.

unsound-contains.superstring.x-detected: {func}({path}, '{literal}') in an if on {attacker_on} is true for values other than '{literal}'
unsound-contains.superstring.x-consequence: an attacker passes the if with a value that the attacker chooses and that has the string at the place that the function checks: for the string alice, the login alice-x passes contains and startsWith, and the login x-alice passes contains and endsWith
unsound-contains.superstring.x-remedy: compare the whole value: the reference == 'the string'

untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref.description: A checkout of the code of a pull request by what its author can move (a branch, refs/pull/<n>/head or merge), in a privileged job that a person approves: the author can push after the approval.

uses.description: The uses of the checkout, as written.

checkout_ref.description: The reference that names what can move, as written: a branch's name with the fork as the repository, refs/pull/<n>/head, or the fork itself.

pr_code_on.description: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.

untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref.x-detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {pr_code_on} after {approval}, and {checkout_ref} can move
untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref.x-consequence: the author pushes after the approval, and the job runs code no one approved with its secrets and its token

uses.description: The uses of the checkout, as written.

checkout_ref.description: The reference that names the pull request's code, as written.

pr_code_on.description: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.

untrusted-checkout.checkout.x-remedy: check out the base's code, or say in a file of facts that the checkout is only read as data

untrusted-checkout.executed.description: A checkout of the code of a pull request, in a privileged job no one approves, which a step after it runs.

uses.description: The uses of the checkout, as written.

checkout_ref.description: The reference that names the pull request's code, as written: a context, such as github.event.pull_request.head.sha, or refs/pull/<n>/merge.

pr_code_on.description: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.

runs.description: The steps after the checkout that run the checked out code: for each step, the name of the step, or steps[<n>] when the step has no name, with n counted from 0 among all the steps of the job or of the action.

untrusted-checkout.executed.x-detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {pr_code_on}, and {runs} runs it
untrusted-checkout.executed.x-consequence: the pull request's author runs their code with the job's secrets and its token
untrusted-checkout.executed.x-remedy: check out the base's code, or run the pull request's code in a pull_request workflow and pass only data to a privileged one

uses-path.outside-repository.description: A uses of another repository, or a $/ uses, whose path goes with .. above the root of the repository.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

uses-path.outside-repository.x-detected: the path of the uses {uses} goes with .. above the root of the repository that the uses names
uses-path.outside-repository.x-consequence: the runner puts each action that the job downloads in _actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref> on the runner, and runs the action of the directory that the path names, outside the repository that the uses names. When another uses of the job, or of a composite action that the job uses, downloads an action into that directory, the step runs that action; when no uses does, the job fails before the steps of the job run. The ref after @ does not decide the code that runs. For a uses of another repository whose path stays in _actions, commit-sha reports, on this step, the ref of the action that runs when that ref is not a full commit SHA
uses-path.outside-repository.x-remedy: write a uses of the action that is meant to run, as owner/repo/path@ref of that action (/path only when the action is in a directory of the repository), without ..

uses-path.outside-workspace.description: A ./ uses whose path goes with .. above the root of the workspace.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

uses-path.outside-workspace.x-detected: the path of the uses {uses} goes with .. above the root of the workspace
uses-path.outside-workspace.x-consequence: the runner resolves the path from the workspace of the job; a ./ uses of an action.yml is resolved from the workspace of the job that runs the action, too. The .. takes the path to a directory of the runner above the workspace, so the step runs an action of the checked-out repository only when the path comes back into the workspace through the name of the directory of the workspace; otherwise the step runs what earlier steps and the runner put in another directory of the runner
uses-path.outside-workspace.x-remedy: write ./ and the path of the action from the root of the workspace, without ..

uses-path.unnormalized-path.description: A uses whose owner, repository or path has parts that GitHub drops or resolves: empty parts (such as // or a / before @), a part that is . or .., or, in a uses of another repository, a backslash.

uses.description: The uses, as written.

normalized.description: The uses as GitHub reads the uses: empty parts dropped, . and .. resolved, a backslash read as /.

uses-path.unnormalized-path.x-detected: the uses {uses} has parts that GitHub drops or resolves, and GitHub reads the uses as {normalized}
uses-path.unnormalized-path.x-consequence: GitHub runs the action of the uses as GitHub reads the uses, not as the uses is written; a person or a tool that reads the uses as written may take the uses for a different action
uses-path.unnormalized-path.x-remedy: write the uses as GitHub reads the uses: no empty part, no part that is . or .. (the ./ at the start of a local action stays), and / between the parts
